short: Scottish engineer who fundamentally improved the steam engine, driving the Industrial Revolution.
full:
James Watt was working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow when he was asked to repair a Newcomen steam engine. Recognising its gross inefficiency, he conceived the idea of a separate condenser in 1765, which allowed the main cylinder to remain hot and dramatically reduced the fuel required to operate it.

Partnering with the industrialist Matthew Boulton in 1775, Watt turned his design into a commercial success that transformed British manufacturing. His subsequent innovations, including the rotary motion gear and the double-acting engine, liberated factories from the need for water power and accelerated the transition to a mechanised, urban industrial economy.
